record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.context_brief: kneading sequences for Hénon maps in WY
record.original_question: For the Hénon maps H_{a,b} in the Wang–Young parameter set WY, describe the kneading set K of all kneading sequences.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. — Describe the set of kneading sequences K of the Hénon map Ha,b, with (a, b) ∈ WY.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Hénon family of diffeomorphisms of the plane
\[ H_{a,b}(x,y) = (1 - a x^2 + y,\; b x), \qquad (a,b)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^*, \]
and let WY denote the Wang–Young parameter set: the positive-measure set of parameters (a,b) with b sufficiently small for which H_{a,b} admits a strange attractor Ω with a unique SRB measure, satisfying the Wang–Young conditions (a strongly dissipative, non-uniformly hyperbolic regime with controlled critical structure, generalizing the Benedicks–Carleson parameters).

For (a,b) ∈ WY, a kneading theory can be developed: to each "critical-like" point z on the attractor one associates a kneading sequence κ(z) ∈ {0,1}^{ℕ} that records the combinatorial itinerary of its forward orbit with respect to a canonical partition of the attractor into two pieces determined by the folding geometry. The kneading set of H_{a,b} is
\[ K(a,b) := \{\kappa(z) : z \text{ is a critical-like point of } H_{a,b}\} \subset \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}. \]

Problem. Give an explicit combinatorial/topological description of the kneading set K(a,b) for Hénon maps H_{a,b} with (a,b) ∈ WY. Equivalently, characterize precisely which subsets of {0,1}^{ℕ} arise as the kneading set of some Hénon map in the Wang–Young regime, and describe the internal structure (admissibility rules, shift-invariance properties, ordering, and dependence on parameters) of such sets.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has developed a kneading theory for Hénon maps in the Wang–Young parameter regime, including a pruning-front-type classification showing that two such Hénon attractors are conjugate iff their kneading sets (equivalently, their folding patterns) coincide. However, a full intrinsic description of which sequences appear in K(a,b) — an analogue of the Milnor–Thurston admissibility characterization for unimodal maps — does not appear in the literature; the problem is posed as open in the list of Hénon-map problems and remains so.

status_evidence.title: The pruning front conjecture, folding patterns and classification of Hénon maps in the presence of strange attractors
status_evidence.snippet: Two Hénon maps are conjugate on their strange attractors iff their sets of kneading sequences coincide, iff their folding patterns coincide.
status_evidence.claim: Kneading theory in WY exists and classifies attractors up to conjugacy, but an intrinsic description of K is not given.

status_evidence.title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 3. — Describe the set of kneading sequences K of the Hénon map Ha,b, with (a, b) ∈ WY.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in a 2023 compilation of Hénon-map open problems.

status_evidence.title: Kneading sequences for toy models of Hénon maps
status_evidence.snippet: Kneading sequences are studied for toy models of Hénon maps.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial/toy-model results are available for related kneading questions.
